dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every real x and t, both partial derivatives of q exist and satisfy q_t + speed • q_x = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The differentiable-initial-profile branch concludes this pointwise equation everywhere, with scalar real values.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: There exist real eigenvalues indexed by ι and an ι-indexed real basis of ι → Real such that the coefficient matrix sends each basis vector to its indexed eigenvalue times that vector.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Asserts a real eigenbasis for the one-by-one matrix [speed]. The eigenvalues and basis may depend on speed.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Every spatial slice is integrable on every bounded interval; every fixed-position flux trace is integrable on every bounded time interval; and the difference of spatial integrals at times t and s equals the time integral from s to t of flux at a minus flux at b, for all real a,b,s,t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The integrable-initial-profile branch concludes all three requirements for flux(state) = speed * state.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For all real x,t, q(x + speed*t,t) = q(x,0).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The common hypothesis of the two regularity branches fixes q along every straight characteristic; equivalently q(x,t) = q(x-speed*t,0).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The matrix indexed by Fin 1 in both coordinates whose sole entry is speed.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the system dimension to one and its coefficient matrix to [speed].

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: An abbreviation for LocalDef009 for a Fin m-indexed vector-valued function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The left side of the equivalence is the vector partial-derivative equation instantiated at m = 1.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: An abbreviation for LocalDef010 with real-valued q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The right side of the equivalence requires the two scalar partial derivatives to exist and obey q_t + speed*q_x = 0.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: Embeds q into Fin 1 → Real by assigning q(x,t) to its unique coordinate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Identifies the scalar field with a one-component vector field in the equivalence.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: There exist vectors qt and qx that are respectively the derivatives of the time and space slices at t and x, and qt + coefficient.mulVec(qx) = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The vector equation includes derivative existence, with witnesses depending on q, the coefficient, x and t.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: There exist qt,qx in the real normed vector space E such that the time slice has derivative qt at t, the space slice has derivative qx at x, and qt + speed • qx = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the scalar equation and the everywhere equation after specializing E to Real; witnesses may vary with x and t.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real scalar multiplication on a real-valued function space is jointly continuous.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the continuity structure used for derivatives of the one-component vector field; adds no hypothesis on q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: Scalar multiplication on any real normed vector space is jointly continuous.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies a structural prerequisite for scalar derivatives; imposes no additional regularity assumption on q.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A structural conversion preserving real multiplication and its scalar action.

dependency_coverage.name: Semiring.toNonUnitalSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains semiring addition and multiplication while forgetting the designated multiplicative identity.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the finite arithmetic of matrix-vector products.

dependency_coverage.name: SubNegZeroMonoid.toNegZeroClass
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains zero, negation and the fact that negation fixes zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the canonical zero used in the scalar derivative equation.

dependency_coverage.name: SubtractionCommMonoid.toSubtractionMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forgets additive commutativity while retaining the subtraction structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Part of the unchanged additive and zero structure of scalar derivative values.

dependency_coverage.name: SubtractionMonoid.toSubNegZeroMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Builds subtraction and negation structure including the law that negation fixes zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the standard zero through the additive structure used by the scalar predicate.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains commutative addition and zero while forgetting inverses as requirements.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports module and vector addition with the original operations.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommGroup.toAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the additive group while forgetting commutativity as a requirement.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies subtraction-related structures for the same real and vector values.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommMonoid.toAddMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains addition and zero while forgetting commutativity as a requirement.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports scalar-action and zero structures without altering the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: ContinuousSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Joint continuity of the map (scalar,vector) ↦ scalar • vector.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: A structural prerequisite for the derivative predicates, supplied automatically for the scalar and function spaces.

dependency_coverage.name: DistribMulAction.toMulAction
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the monoid scalar action while forgetting its additive distributivity as a requirement.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Preserves the real scalar action used in the derivative predicates.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toSemigroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains associative multiplication while forgetting the identity as a requirement.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports inherited real scalar-action structures.

dependency_coverage.name: MonoidWithZero.toMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the multiplicative monoid while forgetting the absorbing-zero requirement.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the same real multiplicative action; does not exclude speed zero.

dependency_coverage.name: MulAction.toSemigroupAction
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains a semigroup action from a monoid action.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Part of the structure path yielding real scalar multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedField.toNormedCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the commutative ring, norm and metric of a normed field.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Ensures the analytic and arithmetic structures inherited from the real field agree.

dependency_coverage.name: Pi.instSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Scalar multiplication of functions is pointwise: (a • f)(i)=a • f(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Eigenvalue multiplication of vectors and scalar actions on vector derivatives operate coordinatewise.

dependency_coverage.name: SemigroupAction.toSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the scalar multiplication operation from a semigroup action.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Yields the same multiplication-based real scalar action used by derivatives.

dependency_coverage.name: SeminormedCommRing.toSeminormedRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: Retains the seminormed ring while forgetting multiplicative commutativity as a requirement.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Preserves the real norm and induced topology along an instance path.

dependency_coverage.name: SeminormedRing.toPseudoMetricSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the compatible pseudometric from a seminormed ring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the usual real topology in scalar multiplication and derivative structures.

dependency_coverage.name: Semiring.toMonoidWithZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts multiplication, identity and absorbing zero from a semiring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the self-module action of Real by multiplication, including speed zero.

dependency_coverage.name: SubNegMonoid.toAddMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts addition and zero from a subtraction-and-negation monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Preserves the additive operations underlying scalar equations and integral differences.

binders: For every speed c ∈ ℝ, the entire conjunction holds.
In the first conjunct there exist λ : Fin 1 → ℝ and a basis e indexed by Fin 1 of the real vector space Fin 1 → ℝ. These witnesses may depend on c; for every p ∈ Fin 1 the eigenvector equation holds.
In the second conjunct, independently quantify every function q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ and every x,t ∈ ℝ.
In the third conjunct, independently quantify every function q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ, then assume the characteristic identity for every real x,t.

The everywhere scalar equation quantifies every real x,t and then existentially quantifies derivative values qt,qx ∈ ℝ at that point. The vector predicate similarly existentially quantifies qt,qx ∈ (Fin 1 → ℝ).

The initial integrability hypothesis quantifies every a,b ∈ ℝ. The integral conclusion quantifies every a,b,t ∈ ℝ for spatial integrability, every x,s,t ∈ ℝ for temporal flux integrability, and every a,b,s,t ∈ ℝ for the balance identity.
The variable state in the flux definition is an arbitrary real input to the fixed function state ↦ c*state.
hypotheses: There is no hypothesis on c and no hypothesis for the eigenbasis assertion or the pointwise equivalence.
The third conjunct assumes q(x+c*t,t)=q(x,0) for every x,t ∈ ℝ.
Under that common hypothesis, the first implication separately assumes that f(x)=q(x,0) is differentiable over ℝ at every x ∈ ℝ.

Under the same common hypothesis, the second implication separately assumes that f(x)=q(x,0) is interval integrable with respect to real volume for every pair a,b ∈ ℝ. The two regularity assumptions are not jointly required.
conclusions: The one-by-one real matrix A=[c] admits a real eigenbasis: there exist λ : Fin 1 → ℝ and a real basis e of Fin 1 → ℝ such that A e(p)=λ(p)e(p) for every p ∈ Fin 1.

For every scalar q and every real point (x,t), let Q(x,t)(0)=q(x,t). There exist vector derivatives Qt of τ ↦ Q(x,τ) at t and Qx of ξ ↦ Q(ξ,t) at x satisfying Qt+A Qx=0 if and only if there exist real derivatives qt of τ ↦ q(x,τ) at t and qx of ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) at x satisfying qt+c*qx=0.
If q satisfies the characteristic identity and its initial profile is everywhere differentiable, then at every real (x,t) both partial derivatives exist and ∂q/∂t(x,t)+c*∂q/∂x(x,t)=0.

If q satisfies the characteristic identity and its initial profile is integrable on every bounded interval, then every spatial slice x ↦ q(x,t) is integrable on every bounded interval, every temporal flux trace τ ↦ c*q(x,τ) is integrable on every bounded interval, and for every real a,b,s,t, ∫_a^b q(x,t) dx − ∫_a^b q(x,s) dx = ∫_s^t [c*q(a,τ) − c*q(b,τ)] dτ. All integrals are oriented interval integrals with respect to real volume.
mathematical_definitions: The independent variables are space x and time t; q is a real-valued state field on all of ℝ², and c is a constant real transport speed.
Fin 1 is the singleton index set {0}; A(0,0)=c and Q(x,t)(0)=q(x,t). Coordinate-vector addition and scalar multiplication are pointwise, with the product topology.
A real eigenbasis is a basis of the full real coordinate space consisting of eigenvectors with real eigenvalues. The proposition does not prescribe a normalization or explicit basis.
The characteristic identity is equivalent, by substituting x−c*t for x, to q(x,t)=f(x−c*t), where f(x)=q(x,0).
The pointwise differential predicates require actual existence of both one-variable slice derivatives and their stated linear relation.
Interval integrability between a and b means integrability on both (a,b] and (b,a]. The interval integral is the integral over (a,b] minus the integral over (b,a], so orientation is retained.
The flux is the fixed linear function F(u)=c*u. The integral balance uses F(q(a,τ))−F(q(b,τ)), in that order.
The real volume appearing in the target is the canonical real measure, conventionally Lebesgue measure.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real constant c, the scalar coefficient matrix [c] has a real eigenbasis, and embedding a real-valued field q as a one-component vector field makes its pointwise vector equation Qt+[c]Qx=0 equivalent to the scalar equation qt+c*qx=0, with existence of both partial derivatives included on each side. Furthermore, any q on all of ℝ² satisfying q(x+c*t,t)=q(x,0) for all real x,t has both of the following conditional properties: if its initial profile is differentiable everywhere, then both partial derivatives exist everywhere and q_t+c*q_x=0 everywhere; if its initial profile is integrable on every bounded interval, then all spatial slices and all fixed-position flux traces are integrable on every bounded interval, and for all real a,b,s,t the change from s to t in the oriented integral of q over a to b equals the oriented time integral of c*q(a,τ)−c*q(b,τ).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The target is restricted to one spatial variable and one scalar state component. Generic vector-space and matrix parameters inside dependencies do not generalize the target to arbitrary systems.
Space and time range over all real numbers, including negative times. There are no spatial boundaries, finite-domain restrictions or nonnegative-time assumptions.
The speed may be positive, negative or zero. At speed zero the characteristic hypothesis makes q independent of time, the flux is zero, and no division by speed is required.

The eigenbasis condition is not vacuous through an empty index set: Fin 1 contains one index and its coordinate space is one-dimensional. No distinct-eigenvalue or orthonormality condition is imposed.

For functions failing the characteristic identity, the third conjunct's implication is vacuous. For functions satisfying it but failing a particular regularity hypothesis, that regularity branch is vacuous.

The pointwise equivalence holds without regularity assumptions; at a point where the required partial derivatives do not exist, both predicates can be false. It does not assert that arbitrary q has partial derivatives.

Differentiability of the initial profile means differentiability everywhere, not continuous differentiability. The differential conclusion explicitly asserts separate slice derivatives and their equation, not continuity of those derivatives.
The integrability assumption is on every bounded interval, not integrability over the whole real line. The integral branch does not require classical differentiability.
The integral conclusion includes integrability requirements, so its content is not merely an identity between potentially default-valued integrals.
Endpoint orders are unrestricted. Equal endpoints make the associated interval integrals zero, but the universally quantified balance is also required for unequal endpoints.
The characteristic identity and balance law hold pointwise for every specified argument, not merely almost everywhere. Boundary fluxes are evaluated at the actual values of q at a and b.

The proposition does not assert a converse from the differential or integral equation to the characteristic identity, an existence theorem for prescribed independent initial data, an entropy condition, or a separate uniqueness theorem.
ambiguities: The dossier leaves standard external semantic boundaries unexpanded, including DifferentiableAt, HasDerivAtFilter, IntegrableOn and the measure selected by the inferInstance body of Real.measureSpace. The translation uses their conventional mathematical meanings; in particular, the supplied body alone does not expose the construction or normalization identifying real volume with Lebesgue measure.
